sources.title: Practical tutorial: Manual flash – distance, power, ISO & aperture
sources.author: Neil van Niekerk
sources.identity: Neil van Niekerk, professional portrait photographer and educator
coverage: aperture and ISO effects on flash exposure
sources.trust_reason: Full instructional article by a working portrait photographer and workshop educator; walks through changing individual flash controls and observing output.
sources.notes: Scope: manual flash and normal-sync behavior; do not generalize shutter independence above sync/HSS.

sources.title: Lighting with Two Speedlights
sources.author: David X. Tejada; Nikon USA editorial presentation
sources.identity: David X. Tejada, professional corporate portrait photographer and workshop instructor
coverage: choose aperture for depth of field
set shutter according to ambient light and handholding
separate ambient and flash test exposures
sources.trust_reason: Full Nikon USA educational article documents Tejada’s actual teaching sequence and rationale, including test exposure and manual power changes.
sources.notes: Nikon CLS product examples; the exposure decisions described are attributed to Tejada. Its same institutional host does not make other Nikon-hosted educators independent when author identity is shared.

sources.title: Photographing Still Life Subjects using Flash
sources.author: Paul Van Allen; Nikon USA editorial presentation
sources.identity: Paul Van Allen, Nikon imaging educator/photographer
coverage: flash and ambient as two exposures
shutter controls ambient in normal flash operation
sources.trust_reason: Full educational article gives a worked real-camera and off-camera Speedlight example and explains the flash/ambient split.
sources.notes: Specific article centers on Nikon Auto FP and still life; use only its general normal-sync light relationship where explicitly stated. Device controls and HSS details remain Nikon/system-specific.

sources.title: Learning How to Use Your Camera's Histogram
sources.author: Nikon USA education team; contributor attribution unclear in article body
coverage: localized playback histogram on supported cameras
sources.trust_reason: Full manufacturer education article describes displayed histogram behavior and recommends selective checks for difficult lighting and series consistency.
sources.notes: The article states supported features vary by camera. RGB/local histogram availability and exact procedures require the user’s camera manual.

sources.title: How to Photograph Snow
sources.author: Canon Editor
sources.identity: Canon U.S.A. camera maker education/support team
coverage: histogram distribution and clipped right edge
sources.trust_reason: Full Canon educational article explains histogram edge behavior using an actual bright-subject use case and clearly ties feature behavior to Canon models and processing.
sources.notes: Snow-specific example illustrates metering and highlight decisions; do not transpose its compensation values to portraits. HTP/RAW handling is Canon-specific.

sources.title: Module 4B: Utilizing the Exposure Triangle to Create Images
sources.author: Professional Photographers of America; page history credits Jessica Avery as creator/editor (original chapter authorship unspecified)
sources.identity: Professional Photographers of America (PPA), trade association and photography education provider
coverage: meter averaging and exposure compensation in bright/dark scenes
limits of camera capture in high contrast
sources.trust_reason: Public full-text chapter in PPA’s Photography Certification Guide gives worked exposure examples and explains subject/background metering trade-offs.
sources.read_depth: full chapter text read; no image pixels inspected
sources.notes: Same institutional family as other PPA chapters; not an independent corroborator of those PPA chapters. Uses Sunny 16 as a starting estimate, not a universal prescription.

sources.title: Awesome Skies: Tips and Techniques for Photographing the Northern Lights
sources.author: Tom Bol; Nikon USA editorial presentation
sources.identity: Tom Bol, professional photographer and workshop leader
coverage: single-channel clipping despite acceptable overall brightness histogram
test exposures in changing ambient light
sources.trust_reason: Full Nikon-hosted article quotes Tom Bol describing his RGB-histogram workflow and the observed green-channel overexposure risk in aurora images.
sources.read_depth: full article; relevant RGB sections read; text only
sources.notes: The observed technique is in aurora color photography; adaptation to saturated cosplay LEDs or costume colors should be tested and not assumed identical. Camera menu details remain model-specific.

gaps: No general source inspected here establishes how every camera’s playback histogram relates to RAW sensor headroom; require model-specific documentation or measurements before making that claim.
